objects.definition:
#ifndef HAVE_TYPE_BYTE
#  undef byte	    /* There might be a macro with this name.  */
#  ifdef __riscos__
     typedef char byte;
#  elif !(defined(_WIN32) && defined(cbNDRContext))
     typedef unsigned char byte;
#  endif
#  define HAVE_TYPE_BYTE
#endif /*!HAVE_TYPE_BYTE*/
objects.description: Alias type for an 8-bit byte. On RISC OS it maps to char; on most other platforms it maps to unsigned char. Defined conditionally to avoid clashes with platform headers (notably some Windows RPC headers).

objects.definition:
#ifndef HAVE_TYPE_USHORT
#  undef ushort     /* There might be a macro with this name.  */
   typedef unsigned short ushort;
#  define HAVE_TYPE_USHORT
#endif
objects.description: Alias for unsigned short, provided for convenience and portability when the platform doesn’t already define it.

objects.definition:
#ifndef HAVE_TYPE_ULONG
#  undef ulong	    /* There might be a macro with this name.  */
   typedef unsigned long ulong;
#  define HAVE_TYPE_ULONG
#endif
objects.description: Alias for unsigned long, provided conditionally for platforms lacking this typedef.

objects.definition:
#ifndef HAVE_TYPE_U16
#  undef u16	    /* There might be a macro with this name.  */
#  if SIZEOF_UNSIGNED_INT == 2
     typedef unsigned int   u16;
#  elif SIZEOF_UNSIGNED_SHORT == 2
     typedef unsigned short u16;
#  else
#    error no typedef for u16
#  endif
#  define HAVE_TYPE_U16
#endif
objects.description: Unsigned 16-bit integer typedef. It resolves to either unsigned int or unsigned short depending on the detected type sizes. Intended to guarantee 16-bit width across platforms.

objects.definition:
#ifndef HAVE_TYPE_U32
#  undef u32        /* There might be a macro with this name.  */
#  if SIZEOF_UNSIGNED_INT == 4
     typedef unsigned int u32;
#  elif SIZEOF_UNSIGNED_LONG == 4
     typedef unsigned long u32;
#  else
#    error no typedef for u32
#  endif
#  define HAVE_TYPE_U32
#endif
objects.description: Unsigned 32-bit integer typedef. It resolves to either unsigned int or unsigned long depending on the detected type sizes. Intended to guarantee 32-bit width across platforms.

functions.name: has_leading_keyword
functions.description: Checks whether the given string begins with the specified keyword and returns a pointer to the position in STRING after the leading keyword (or possibly after surrounding/leading whitespace). Exact matching and whitespace rules are not documented here; behavior is inferred from the name. Returns NULL if KEYWORD is not present at the beginning.
requirements: STRING must be a valid, null-terminated C string.
KEYWORD must be a valid, null-terminated C string.
Returned pointer, if non-NULL, aliases STRING; caller must not free it.
Exact matching rules (case sensitivity, whitespace handling) are unknown from this header.

functions.name: memistr
functions.signature: const char *memistr (const void *buf, size_t buflen, const char *sub);
functions.description: Searches BUF (of length BUFLEN) for the first occurrence of the substring SUB, ignoring ASCII case. Returns a pointer into BUF on success, or NULL if not found. Inferred from name; not explicitly documented here.
requirements: BUF must point to a valid memory region of at least BUFLEN bytes.
SUB must be a valid, null-terminated C string.
Search is case-insensitive for ASCII letters (inferred).
Returned pointer, if non-NULL, points inside BUF; do not free it.

functions.name: gnupg_memstr
functions.signature: const char *gnupg_memstr (const void *buffer, size_t buflen, const char *sub);
functions.description: Searches the memory region BUFFER (length BUFLEN) for the substring SUB (case-sensitive). Returns a pointer to the first match within BUFFER or NULL if not found. Inferred from common naming patterns.
requirements: BUFFER must point to a valid memory region of at least BUFLEN bytes.
SUB must be a valid, null-terminated C string.
Returned pointer, if non-NULL, points inside BUFFER; do not free it.
Case sensitivity is inferred; exact behavior not explicitly documented.

functions.name: mem2str
functions.description: Copies bytes from a memory region into a C string buffer, ensuring NUL termination. The exact copying rules (e.g., stopping at first NUL in source vs copying up to size-1) are not documented here and are inferred from the function name used in GnuPG.
requirements: The first argument must be a writable destination buffer large enough to hold the resulting NUL-terminated string.
The second argument must point to a readable memory region of at least the specified SIZE bytes.
Behavior details (truncation rules, stopping at embedded NULs) are unknown from this header.

functions.name: trim_spaces
functions.description: Trims leading and trailing whitespace from STRING in place and returns STRING (or possibly a pointer into it). The precise return (original vs advanced pointer) is not specified here; inferred from name.
requirements: STRING must be a writable, null-terminated C string.
Trimming is performed in place; the buffer content may be modified and characters may be shifted.
Exact definition of whitespace set is not specified in this header.

functions.name: ascii_trim_spaces
functions.description: Trims leading and trailing ASCII whitespace from STRING in place. Returns a pointer (likely to the start of the trimmed string). ASCII semantics implied by name.
requirements: STRING must be a writable, null-terminated C string.
Operates in place; content may be modified and shifted.
Whitespace definition limited to ASCII (inferred).
Exact return (same pointer vs advanced) not documented here.

functions.name: trim_trailing_spaces
functions.description: Removes trailing whitespace characters from STRING in place. Returns STRING (inferred).
requirements: STRING must be a writable, null-terminated C string.
Operates in place; may write a new NUL terminator.
Exact whitespace set not defined here.

functions.name: trim_trailing_chars
functions.signature: unsigned int trim_trailing_chars( unsigned char *line, unsigned len, const char *trimchars);
functions.description: Removes trailing characters listed in TRIMCHARS from the byte sequence LINE of length LEN. Returns the new length after trimming. Inferred from the function name and parameters.
requirements: LINE must point to a writable buffer of at least LEN bytes.
Function treats LINE as a byte array, not necessarily NUL-terminated.
TRIMCHARS must be a valid, null-terminated C string listing characters to trim.
The function may modify bytes near the end of LINE (e.g., by writing NULs); exact modification semantics are not specified.

functions.name: trim_trailing_ws
functions.signature: unsigned int trim_trailing_ws( unsigned char *line, unsigned len );
functions.description: Removes trailing ASCII whitespace from the byte sequence LINE of length LEN. Returns the new length. Inferred from the name.
requirements: LINE must point to a writable buffer of at least LEN bytes.
Whitespace definition and exact modification semantics are not documented here.

functions.name: length_sans_trailing_chars
functions.signature: size_t length_sans_trailing_chars (const unsigned char *line, size_t len, const char *trimchars );
functions.description: Computes the length of LINE without any trailing characters found in TRIMCHARS, without modifying LINE. Returns the resulting length. Inferred from name.
requirements: LINE must point to at least LEN readable bytes.
TRIMCHARS must be a valid, null-terminated C string.

functions.name: length_sans_trailing_ws
functions.signature: size_t length_sans_trailing_ws (const unsigned char *line, size_t len);
functions.description: Computes the length of LINE after removing trailing whitespace, without modifying LINE. Returns the resulting length. Inferred from name.
requirements: LINE must point to at least LEN readable bytes.
Definition of whitespace not specified here (likely ASCII).

functions.name: make_basename
functions.description: Creates and returns a newly allocated string containing the basename component for FILEPATH, possibly using INPUTPATH as a hint for stripping or normalization (inferred). Exact behavior is not documented here.
requirements: FILEPATH must be a valid, null-terminated path string.
INPUTPATH, if used, must be a valid, null-terminated string; exact role is unspecified here.
Returns a malloc-allocated string on success; caller must free it.
Error and edge-case behavior are not documented in this header.

functions.name: make_dirname
functions.description: Returns a newly allocated string containing the directory portion (dirname) of FILEPATH. Inferred from the name.
requirements: FILEPATH must be a valid, null-terminated path string.
Returns a malloc-allocated string; caller must free it.
Exact handling of root paths, trailing slashes, and errors is not documented here.

functions.name: make_filename
functions.description: Builds a path string by concatenating path components from the variadic arguments. Returns a newly allocated string. The argument list must be terminated by a NULL sentinel as indicated by the attribute. Inferred from naming and common GnuPG helpers.
requirements: FIRST_PART must be a valid, null-terminated string representing the first path component.
Variadic arguments must be a sequence of const char* components terminated by a NULL pointer (per GPGRT_ATTR_SENTINEL(0)).
Returns a malloc-allocated string; caller must free it.
Exact path separator insertion and error handling are not specified here.

functions.name: make_filename_try
functions.description: Like make_filename but returns NULL on memory allocation failure instead of aborting (inferred). Builds a path from variadic components terminated by NULL.
requirements: FIRST_PART must be a valid, null-terminated string.
Variadic arguments must be const char* components terminated by NULL (per sentinel).
On success returns a malloc-allocated string; caller must free it.
Exact path joining rules are not documented here.

functions.name: make_absfilename
functions.description: Creates an absolute pathname by joining variadic components terminated by NULL. Likely ensures the result is absolute (inferred).
requirements: FIRST_PART must be a valid, null-terminated string.
Variadic arguments must be const char* components terminated by NULL (per sentinel).
Returns a malloc-allocated string; caller must free it.
Exact rules for making the path absolute and error handling are not documented here.

functions.name: make_absfilename_try
functions.description: Like make_absfilename but returns NULL on allocation failure (inferred). Joins variadic components to produce an absolute path; list must be NULL-terminated.
requirements: FIRST_PART must be a valid, null-terminated string.
Variadic arguments must be const char* and NULL-terminated (per sentinel).
On success returns a malloc-allocated string; caller must free it.

functions.name: compare_filenames
functions.signature: int compare_filenames( const char *a, const char *b );
functions.description: Compares two filenames A and B using GnuPG’s filename comparison rules (e.g., platform-specific case sensitivity, path normalization). Returns an integer comparison result (inferred).
requirements: A and B must be valid, null-terminated strings.
Exact return convention (negative/zero/positive) and comparison rules are not documented in this header.

functions.name: string_to_u64
functions.description: Parses STRING and returns its numeric value as an unsigned 64-bit integer. Error handling and accepted formats are not documented here; typical behavior would parse decimal (possibly hex) numbers. Inferred from name.
requirements: STRING must be a valid, null-terminated C string.
Behavior on invalid input, overflow, and supported bases is not specified here.

functions.name: hextobyte
functions.description: Converts a textual hexadecimal byte at S to an integer in the range 0–255 (inferred). Error signaling (e.g., negative on error) is not documented here.
requirements: S must point to at least two readable characters representing a hex byte (inferred).
Return-on-error behavior is unspecified in this header.

functions.name: utf8_charcount
functions.description: Counts the number of UTF-8 encoded characters in S, examining up to LEN bytes (or the whole string if LEN indicates so). Exact handling of invalid sequences and special LEN values (e.g., -1) is not documented here. Inferred from name.
requirements: S must point to at least LEN readable bytes if LEN >= 0, or to a null-terminated UTF-8 string if using a sentinel value (inferred).
Behavior on invalid UTF-8 is not specified in this header.

functions.name: w32_strerror
functions.description: Windows-only: Returns a human-readable error message string for the Windows error code EC. Available only when built with HAVE_W32_SYSTEM. The returned pointer likely refers to static or thread-local storage (inferred).
requirements: Only available if HAVE_W32_SYSTEM is defined; not present on non-Windows builds.
EC should be a valid Windows error code.
Ownership of the returned string is unspecified; treat it as non-owning unless documented otherwise.

functions.name: ascii_isupper
functions.description: Returns nonzero if C is an ASCII uppercase letter ('A'–'Z'), zero otherwise. ASCII-only semantics.
requirements: C must be representable as an unsigned char cast to int or EOF, per ctype-like conventions (inferred).

functions.name: ascii_islower
functions.description: Returns nonzero if C is an ASCII lowercase letter ('a'–'z'), zero otherwise. ASCII-only semantics.
requirements: C should be convertible to unsigned char in int range (inferred).

functions.name: ascii_toupper
functions.description: Converts ASCII lowercase letters to uppercase; returns C unchanged for non-lowercase or non-ASCII. ASCII-only semantics.
requirements: Input C should be in the unsigned char range or EOF (inferred).

functions.name: ascii_tolower
functions.description: Converts ASCII uppercase letters to lowercase; returns C unchanged for other characters. ASCII-only semantics.
requirements: Input C should be in the unsigned char range or EOF (inferred).

functions.name: ascii_strlwr
functions.description: Converts all ASCII letters in S to lowercase in place. Returns S.
requirements: S must be a writable, null-terminated C string.
Only ASCII letters are affected.

functions.name: ascii_strupr
functions.description: Converts all ASCII letters in S to uppercase in place. Returns S.
requirements: S must be a writable, null-terminated C string.
Only ASCII letters are affected.

functions.name: ascii_strcasecmp
functions.signature: int ascii_strcasecmp( const char *a, const char *b );
functions.description: Compares two strings case-insensitively using ASCII rules. Returns an integer less than, equal to, or greater than zero, similar to strcasecmp (inferred).
requirements: A and B must be valid, null-terminated strings.
Comparison is ASCII-only; behavior for non-ASCII bytes is deterministic but not locale-aware.

functions.name: ascii_strncasecmp
functions.signature: int ascii_strncasecmp (const char *a, const char *b, size_t n);
functions.description: Compares up to N characters of A and B case-insensitively using ASCII rules. Return convention like strncasecmp (inferred).
requirements: A and B must be valid, null-terminated strings (or at least N bytes readable).
ASCII-only, non-locale-aware comparison.

functions.name: ascii_memcasecmp
functions.signature: int ascii_memcasecmp( const void *a, const void *b, size_t n );
functions.description: Case-insensitive comparison of two memory regions A and B of length N using ASCII rules. Returns an integer comparison result (inferred).
requirements: A and B must point to readable memory regions of at least N bytes.
Case-insensitivity applies only to ASCII letters.

functions.name: ascii_memistr
functions.signature: const char *ascii_memistr ( const void *buf, size_t buflen, const char *sub);
functions.description: Searches BUF (BUFLEN bytes) for SUB case-insensitively using ASCII rules. Returns pointer to first match within BUF, or NULL if not found. Equivalent in spirit to memistr (naming suggests ASCII emphasis).
requirements: BUF must be a valid memory region of at least BUFLEN bytes.
SUB must be a valid, null-terminated C string.
Returned pointer, if non-NULL, points inside BUF and must not be freed.

functions.name: ascii_memcasemem
functions.signature: void *ascii_memcasemem (const void *haystack, size_t nhaystack, const void *needle, size_t nneedle);
functions.description: Searches HAYSTACK (NHAYSTACK bytes) for the byte sequence NEEDLE (NNEEDLE bytes) ignoring ASCII case for letters. Returns pointer to first match within HAYSTACK or NULL if not found. Inferred from name.
requirements: HAYSTACK must point to a readable memory region of at least NHAYSTACK bytes.
NEEDLE must point to a readable memory region of at least NNEEDLE bytes; NNEEDLE should be > 0 for a meaningful search.
Returned pointer, if non-NULL, points inside HAYSTACK and must not be freed.

functions.name: memicmp
functions.signature: int memicmp( const char *a, const char *b, size_t n );
functions.description: Case-insensitive comparison of the first N bytes of A and B using ASCII semantics. Provided only if the system lacks memicmp. Returns integer less than, equal to, or greater than zero. Inferred from standard behavior.
requirements: Only available when HAVE_MEMICMP is not defined (otherwise use the system’s function).
A and B must point to readable memory regions of at least N bytes.

functions.name: stpcpy
functions.description: Copies string B (including terminating NUL) into buffer A and returns a pointer to the terminating NUL in A. Declared here only if the system lacks stpcpy.
requirements: Only available when HAVE_STPCPY is not defined (otherwise use the system’s function).
A must be a writable buffer large enough to hold B including the NUL terminator.
B must be a valid, null-terminated string.

functions.name: strpbrk
functions.description: Finds the first character in S that matches any character in ACCEPT. Returns a pointer to that character, or NULL if none. Declared only if the system lacks strpbrk.
requirements: Only available when HAVE_STRPBRK is not defined (otherwise use the system’s function).
S and ACCEPT must be valid, null-terminated C strings.

functions.name: strsep
functions.description: Tokenizes the string referenced by *STRINGP by delimiting characters in DELIM, returning the next token and updating *STRINGP. Declared only if the system lacks strsep. Standard BSD behavior is implied by the name.
requirements: Only available when HAVE_STRSEP is not defined (otherwise use the system’s function).
STRINGP must be non-NULL and point to a char* that is either NULL or a modifiable, null-terminated string buffer.
DELIM must be a valid, null-terminated string of delimiter characters.
May write NULs into the string to terminate tokens.

functions.name: strlwr
functions.description: Converts the string A to lowercase in place and returns A. Declared only if the system lacks strlwr. Nonstandard function; ASCII semantics implied.
requirements: Only available when HAVE_STRLWR is not defined (otherwise use the system’s function).
A must be a writable, null-terminated string.
Exact locale/Unicode handling is not specified; typically ASCII.

functions.name: memrchr
functions.signature: void *memrchr (const void *buffer, int c, size_t n);
functions.description: Searches the last N bytes of BUFFER for the last occurrence of byte C. Returns a pointer to the matching byte, or NULL if not found. Declared only if the system lacks memrchr.
requirements: Only available when HAVE_MEMRCHR is not defined (otherwise use the system’s function).
BUFFER must point to at least N readable bytes.
C is interpreted as an unsigned char value.

functions.name: percent_escape
functions.description: Percent-escapes STR by replacing ':' with "%3a" and, if EXTRA is not NULL, also escapes any characters listed in EXTRA. Returns a newly allocated string. Documented in the header comment.
requirements: STR must be a valid, null-terminated string.
EXTRA may be NULL or a valid, null-terminated string of additional characters to escape.
Returns a malloc-allocated string; caller must free it.
On allocation failure, behavior is to return a string (non-try variant); exact failure mode not specified beyond that try_ variant returns NULL.

functions.name: try_percent_escape
functions.description: Like percent_escape but returns NULL if not enough memory can be allocated. Documented in the header comment.
requirements: STR must be a valid, null-terminated string.
EXTRA may be NULL or a valid, null-terminated string.
On success returns a malloc-allocated string; caller must free it.
Returns NULL on memory allocation failure.

functions.name: strconcat
functions.description: Concatenates S1 with all following strings up to a NULL, returning a newly allocated string. Returns NULL on malloc error or if too many arguments are given. Documented in the header comment.
requirements: S1 must be a valid, null-terminated string.
Variadic arguments must be a sequence of const char* terminated by NULL (per sentinel).
Returns a malloc-allocated string on success; caller must free it.
May return NULL on memory error or if the argument list is excessively long (as per implementation).

functions.name: vstrconcat
functions.description: Variadic-list version of strconcat. Concatenates S1 with subsequent strings from ARG_PTR until a NULL is encountered; returns a newly allocated string or NULL on error. Documented in the header comment.
requirements: S1 must be a valid, null-terminated string.
ARG_PTR must be a valid va_list initialized to a sequence of const char* arguments terminated by a NULL pointer.
Returns a malloc-allocated string on success; caller must free it.
May return NULL on memory error.

functions.name: xstrconcat
functions.description: Like strconcat but dies (aborts/exits) on error. Concatenates S1 with subsequent strings up to a NULL sentinel and returns a newly allocated string. Documented in the header comment.
requirements: S1 must be a valid, null-terminated string.
Variadic arguments must be const char* terminated by NULL (per sentinel).
Returns a malloc-allocated string; caller must free it.
Will terminate the process on allocation failure (do not rely on NULL).

functions.name: strsplit
functions.signature: char **strsplit (char *string, char delim, char replacement, int *count);
functions.description: Splits STRING into tokens on delimiter DELIM, optionally replacing the delimiter with REPLACEMENT in the original buffer, and returns an array of pointers to tokens. COUNT, if non-NULL, receives the number of tokens. Inferred from parameters; details not fully documented here.
requirements: STRING must be a writable, null-terminated string buffer; function may modify it in place.
DELIM specifies the delimiter character; REPLACEMENT is the character written in place of delimiters (inferred).
COUNT may be NULL or a valid pointer to int to receive the token count.
Return is likely a malloc-allocated array; ownership and freeing rules are not specified in this header.

functions.description: Tokenizes STRING using the set of delimiter characters in DELIM. Trims tokens (per comment). Returns a list/array of tokens. Exact allocation and termination details are not documented here.
requirements: STRING and DELIM must be valid, null-terminated strings.
Returns dynamically allocated storage; caller likely must free tokens/array, but exact ownership rules are not specified.

functions.name: strtokenize_nt
functions.description: Like strtokenize but does not trim tokens (per comment). Returns an array of tokens. Allocation and ownership details are not documented here.
requirements: STRING and DELIM must be valid, null-terminated strings.
Returns dynamically allocated storage; caller likely must free it (unspecified here).

functions.name: split_fields
functions.signature: int split_fields (char *string, const char **array, int arraysize);
functions.description: Splits STRING into space-delimited fields and stores pointers to fields in ARRAY up to ARRAYSIZE. Returns the number of fields stored (inferred from comment).
requirements: STRING must be a writable, null-terminated string; function may write NUL terminators into it.
ARRAY must point to storage for at least ARRAYSIZE pointers.
ARRAYSIZE must be non-negative.
Exact return on truncation (more fields than ARRAYSIZE) is not specified here.

functions.name: split_fields_colon
functions.signature: int split_fields_colon (char *string, const char **array, int arraysize);
functions.description: Splits STRING into colon ':' delimited fields and stores pointers in ARRAY up to ARRAYSIZE. Returns the number of fields stored (inferred).
requirements: STRING must be a writable, null-terminated string; function may write NUL terminators.
ARRAY must point to storage for at least ARRAYSIZE pointers.
ARRAYSIZE must be non-negative.

functions.name: compare_version_strings
functions.description: Returns true (nonzero) if MY_VERSION is greater than or equal to REQ_VERSION (per comment). Implements version string comparison under GnuPG’s rules.
requirements: MY_VERSION and REQ_VERSION must be valid, null-terminated strings representing versions.
Return is a boolean-style int (nonzero for >=); exact handling of malformed versions is not documented here.

functions.name: format_text
functions.signature: char *format_text (const char *text, int target_cols, int max_cols);
functions.description: Formats TEXT to wrap to approximately TARGET_COLS columns, with a constraint given by MAX_COLS. Returns a newly allocated formatted string (per comment).
requirements: TEXT must be a valid, null-terminated string.
TARGET_COLS and MAX_COLS should be positive; exact accepted ranges are not documented here.
Returns a malloc-allocated string; caller must free it.

functions.name: replace_substr
functions.signature: char *replace_substr (const char *string, const char *substr, const char *replace);
functions.description: Returns a new malloced string with the first occurrence of SUBSTR in STRING replaced by REPLACE. Returns NULL on memory error (per comment).
requirements: STRING, SUBSTR, and REPLACE must be valid, null-terminated strings.
Returns a malloc-allocated string on success; caller must free it.
Returns NULL on memory allocation failure.
If SUBSTR is not found, behavior (returning a copy vs returning STRING) is not specified here.

functions.signature: char *substitute_vars (const char *string, const char *(*getval)(void *cookie, const char *name), void *cookie);
functions.description: Substitutes variables in STRING using callback GETVAL, which receives COOKIE and a variable NAME and returns the replacement string. Returns a newly allocated string with substitutions applied. Documented by the comment header.
requirements: STRING must be a valid, null-terminated string containing variable placeholders (exact syntax not specified here).

GETVAL must be a valid function pointer; it will be called with COOKIE and variable names. It must return a valid, null-terminated string for found variables; behavior for unknown variables is unspecified here.
Returns a malloc-allocated string; caller must free it.
Error handling (e.g., allocation failures, callback returning NULL) is not specified in this header.

functions.name: substitute_envvars
functions.description: Substitutes environment-variable references in STRING and returns a newly allocated result. Documented in the header comment.
requirements: STRING must be a valid, null-terminated string.
Environment variable syntax and platform-specific behavior are not specified here.
Returns a malloc-allocated string; caller must free it.

functions.description: Maps STRING using a static macro string table and returns the mapped constant string, or STRING/unmodified if not found (inferred). Intended to avoid allocations. Behavior details are not documented here.
requirements: STRING must be a valid, null-terminated string.
Returned pointer is not owned by the caller; do not free it.

data_types.description: A generic null-terminated C string containing arbitrary text; may include whitespace and non-ASCII bytes. Intended for functions that treat input as human-readable text.
A null-terminated string intended to be matched as a leading keyword or token in another string. Typically alphabetic, but fuzzing may include any bytes.
A byte sequence that may contain any values including NUL bytes; not required to be null-terminated. Used when functions operate on buffers with explicit lengths.

    extras = ''.join(rng.choice(string.printable.strip()) for _ in range(rng.randint(0, 4)))
    out = (s + extras)
    # Remove duplicates while preserving order
    seen = set()
    uniq = []
    for ch in out:
        if ch not in seen:
            seen.add(ch)
            uniq.append(ch)
    return ''.join(uniq).encode('ascii', 'ignore')


def _utf8_sample(rng: random.Random, min_len: int, max_len: int) -> bytes:
    # Mix ASCII and some multi-byte UTF-8 sequences
    ascii_part = _rand_ascii_text(rng, min_len // 2, max_len // 2)
    # Some common multi-byte sequences
    multibyte = [
        "ä", "ö", "ü", "ß", "é", "è", "ê", "à", "€", "™", "✓", "漢", "字", "🙂"
    ]
    k = rng.randint(2, 8)
    mb = ''.join(rng.choice(multibyte) for _ in range(k)).encode('utf-8')
    s = ascii_part + mb
    if len(s) > max_len:
        s = s[:max_len]
    return s


def _path_like(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    base = rng.choice(PATH_SAMPLES)
    # splice in random components
    comps = [base]
    for _ in range(rng.randint(0, 3)):
        part = rng.choice(WORDS).lower()
        if rng.random() < 0.3:
            part += "." + rng.choice(["txt", "conf", "bin", "exe"])
        comps.append(part)
    # Join with slashes/backslashes variety to exercise comparisons on different platforms
    sep = rng.choice(["/", "\\\\"])  # literal backslashes
    s = sep.join(comps)
    return s.encode('utf-8', 'ignore')


def _pack_record(t: int, payload: bytes) -> bytes:
    # Record: 1 byte type, 2 bytes length (little-endian), followed by payload
    n = len(payload)
    if n > 0xFFFF:
        payload = payload[:0xFFFF]
        n = len(payload)
    return bytes([t & 0xFF]) + bytes([n & 0xFF, (n >> 8) & 0xFF]) + payload


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    records: List[bytes] = []

    # Ensure presence of key pairs for haystack/needle, trim sets, etc.
    # 1) ASCII text block (good for case-insensitive search and trimming)
    records.append(_pack_record(0x01, _rand_ascii_text(rng, 16, 96)))

    # 2) Binary haystack with NULs
    records.append(_pack_record(0x02, _rand_binary(rng, 32, 256)))

    # 3) Needle for searches (kept short)
    records.append(_pack_record(0x03, _rand_needle(rng, 32)))

    # 4) Whitespace tail string
    records.append(_pack_record(0x04, _whitespace_tail(rng, 8, 48)))

    # 5) Trimchars set
    records.append(_pack_record(0x05, _trimchars_set(rng)))

    # 6) UTF-8 rich text
    records.append(_pack_record(0x06, _utf8_sample(rng, 8, 128)))

    # 7) Path-like strings
    records.append(_pack_record(0x07, _path_like(rng)))

    # Additional variability: add a few more mixed records
    extra_count = rng.randint(3, 7)
    for _ in range(extra_count):
        t = rng.choice([0x01, 0x02, 0x03, 0x04, 0x05])
        if t == 0x01:
            payload = _rand_ascii_text(rng, 4, 64)
        elif t == 0x02:
            payload = _rand_binary(rng, 8, 128)
        elif t == 0x03:
            payload = _rand_needle(rng, 24)
        elif t == 0x04:
            payload = _whitespace_tail(rng, 4, 32)
        else:
            payload = _trimchars_set(rng)
        records.append(_pack_record(t, payload))

    # Concatenate while respecting 4096 limit
    out = bytearray()
    for rec in records:
        if len(out) + len(rec) > 4096:
            break
        out.extend(rec)

    return bytes(out)

import random
import string
from typing import List

# Generator for ASCII-oriented fuzz stubs. We create a corpus entry containing
# several concatenated NUL-terminated strings so FUZZ_PARAM_STR() can slice
# interesting values. The fuzzing harness typically pulls sequential blobs
# from the buffer; providing a variety of strings increases coverage.
#
# We include:
# - Pure whitespace variants (leading/trailing/mixed) to exercise trimming.
# - Case-mixed words and sentences for case-folding/strcasecmp paths.
# - Repeated patterns for substring search (ascii_memistr).
# - Edge cases: empty strings, NUL-only, all ASCII classes, punctuation.
# - Variable lengths, including 0 and up to about 1k to match stub caps.
# - Tokens with different delimiters that might be reused across calls.
#
# The output is a single bytes object consisting of multiple C strings
# concatenated back-to-back, each NUL-terminated, and overall <= 4096 bytes.

ASCII_WS = "\t\n\x0b\x0c\r "
PRINTABLE = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + string.punctuation + " "


def _rand_choice(rng: random.Random, seq: List[str]):
    return seq[rng.randrange(len(seq))]


def _rand_ws(rng: random.Random, min_len=0, max_len=32):
    n = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    return "".join(rng.choice(ASCII_WS) for _ in range(n))


def _random_printable(rng: random.Random, min_len=0, max_len=64):
    n = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    return "".join(rng.choice(PRINTABLE) for _ in range(n))


def _mixed_case(rng: random.Random, s: str) -> str:
    out = []
    for ch in s:
        if ch.isalpha():
            out.append(ch.upper() if rng.random() < 0.5 else ch.lower())
        else:
            out.append(ch)
    return "".join(out)


def _pattern_block(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Create a haystack with repeated case-varied pattern occurrences.
    base = _rand_choice(rng, ["alpha", "Beta", "Gamma", "delta", "TEST", "case", "Space", "Line"])  # candidate
    pat = _mixed_case(rng, base)
    parts = []
    # Interleave noise and pattern in varying cases
    for _ in range(rng.randint(2, 8)):
        parts.append(_random_printable(rng, 0, rng.randint(0, 24)))
        parts.append(_mixed_case(rng, pat))
    parts.append(_random_printable(rng, 0, 24))
    s = "".join(parts)
    # Limit to ~512 for stub cap comfort
    return s[:512]


def _alpha_sequences(rng: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    # Common targets for search and compare
    tokens = [
        "HelloWorld",
        "helloworld",
        "HeLLoWoRLD",
        "ASCII",
        "ascii",
        "CaseInsensitive",
        "caseinsensitive",
        "TeStInG",
        "",  # empty
    ]
    # Add random mixed words
    for _ in range(5):
        word = _random_printable(rng, 3, 16)
        tokens.append(_mixed_case(rng, word))
    return tokens


def _whitespace_variants(rng: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    samples = []
    core_tokens = [
        "",  # pure empty
        "a",
        "A",
        "abc",
        "ABC",
        "Mixed Case String",
        "Tabs\tAnd\tSpaces",
        "Newlines\nAnd\rReturns",
    ]
    for t in core_tokens:
        samples.append(t)
        samples.append(_rand_ws(rng, 1, 8) + t)
        samples.append(t + _rand_ws(rng, 1, 8))
        samples.append(_rand_ws(rng, 1, 8) + t + _rand_ws(rng, 1, 8))
    # Also include strings of only whitespace (various lengths)
    for n in [0, 1, 2, 3, 7, 16, 31, 64]:
        samples.append(_rand_ws(rng, n, n))
    return samples


def _punct_sets() -> List[str]:
    # Include various punctuation sets useful for token/accept searches.
    punct = [
        "!@#$%^&*()",
        "[]{}<>",
        ",.;:?!",
        "'\"`~",
        "-_=+|/\\",
    ]
    return punct


def _lengthy_sentence(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    base = (
        "Lorem ipsum DOLOR sit amet, consectetur adipiscing elit. "
        "Vestibulum	vitae\nNIBH\r\nquis massa gravida posuere."
    )
    s = _mixed_case(rng, base)
    # Randomly add leading/trailing spaces
    return _rand_ws(rng, 0, 6) + s + _rand_ws(rng, 0, 6)


def _build_strings(rng: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    pieces: List[str] = []

    # Edge cases
    pieces.append("")                # empty string
    pieces.append("\x00")             # this will be truncated at first NUL when consumed

    # Whitespace-focused for trimming
    pieces.extend(_whitespace_variants(rng))

    # Case transformations
    pieces.extend(_alpha_sequences(rng))

    # Punctuation-heavy strings
    pieces.extend(_punct_sets())

    # Repeated patterns for memistr/ascii_memistr
    for _ in range(4):
        pieces.append(_pattern_block(rng))

    # Sentences and random blocks
    pieces.append(_lengthy_sentence(rng))
    for _ in range(5):
        pieces.append(_random_printable(rng, 0, 80))

    # Specific interesting substrings
    pieces.extend([
        "TeSt",  # for case-insensitive find/compare
        "test",
        "TEST",
        "space space",
        "  leading",
        "trailing  ",
        "\t\n mix \r\f",
    ])

    # Ensure some very short and very long within 1k
    pieces.append(_random_printable(rng, 256, 512))
    pieces.append(_random_printable(rng, 800, 1000))

    # Deduplicate modestly while preserving order
    seen = set()
    uniq = []
    for s in pieces:
        if s not in seen:
            seen.add(s)
            uniq.append(s)
    return uniq


essential_min = 16  # ensure at least some content


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    strings = _build_strings(rng)

    # Randomly shuffle a subset to vary ordering per seed
    rng.shuffle(strings)

    # Serialize as NUL-terminated C strings back-to-back.
    out = bytearray()
    for s in strings:
        # Cap individual strings to 1024 to match fuzzer allocations
        b = s.encode('latin-1', errors='ignore')[:1024]
        out += b + b"\x00"
        if len(out) > 4000:  # keep under 4096 total
            break

    # Guarantee non-empty
    if not out:
        out = bytearray(b"\x00")

    # Ensure minimum
    while len(out) < essential_min:
        extra = _random_printable(rng, 0, 8).encode('latin-1', errors='ignore') + b"\x00"
        out += extra

    return bytes(out)

import random
import string
from typing import List

# This generator targets functions that take NUL-terminated C-strings, often
# as general text plus a "character set string" specifying delimiters or
# characters-to-trim. The fuzzer harness uses FUZZ_PARAM_STR to fetch such
# inputs. We therefore produce a single bytes buffer that contains several
# NUL-terminated strings concatenated. The harness will slice them for
# multiple FUZZ_PARAM_STR calls.
#
# Layout we produce (all parts are ASCII/UTF-8 compatible):
#   [S0]\0[S1]\0[S2]\0[S3]\0
# Where:
# - S0: General text payload (lines, fields, colons, spaces, UTF-8, edge chars)
# - S1: Trim set (characters to be trimmed at end) for trim_* functions
# - S2: Delimiter set (for strsep/strpbrk/strtokenize[_nt])
# - S3: Extra escape set for percent_escape/try_percent_escape
#
# We aim for valid and interesting inputs that exercise:
# - Trailing whitespace vs custom trim chars
# - Empty strings and strings with only delimiters
# - Mixed ASCII cases, punctuation, control chars, and UTF-8 multibyte sequences
# - Presence/absence of ':' for percent_escape
# - Long and short tokens, repeated delimiters, and edge cases like leading/trailing delimiters
#
# The buffer stays under 4096 bytes.

ASCII_WHITESPACE = " \t\r\n\v\f"
COMMON_DELIMS = ",;:|/\\\t \n\r\0"
PUNCT = "!@#$%^&*()_+-={}[]""|:;<>,.?/\\'\""
HEX = "0123456789abcdefABCDEF"
WORD_CHARS = string.ascii_letters + string.digits

# Some UTF-8 sequences (valid multibyte characters) to mix in
UTF8_SNIPPETS = [
    "π", "✓", "é", "ñ", "漢", "字", "🙂", "€", "—", "·",
]

def _rand_from(rng: random.Random, s: str, k: int) -> str:
    return ''.join(rng.choice(s) for _ in range(k))

def _maybe(rng: random.Random, p: float) -> bool:
    return rng.random() < p

def _make_general_text(rng: random.Random, target_len: int) -> str:
    parts: List[str] = []

    # Start with optional leading spaces/newlines
    if _maybe(rng, 0.7):
        parts.append(_rand_from(rng, ASCII_WHITESPACE, rng.randint(0, 8)))

    # Add some fields separated by mixed delimiters
    fields = []
    n_fields = rng.randint(1, 8)
    for i in range(n_fields):
        frag = []
        # Optional leading delimiter in field
        if _maybe(rng, 0.3):
            frag.append(rng.choice(COMMON_DELIMS[:-1]))
        # Core token with words, punctuation, and occasional UTF-8
        core_len = rng.randint(1, 20)
        for _ in range(core_len):
            choice = rng.random()
            if choice < 0.6:
                frag.append(rng.choice(WORD_CHARS))
            elif choice < 0.8:
                frag.append(rng.choice(PUNCT))
            elif choice < 0.9:
                frag.append(rng.choice(ASCII_WHITESPACE))
            else:
                frag.append(rng.choice(UTF8_SNIPPETS))
        # Optional hex-like snippet to tickle hextobyte searches elsewhere
        if _maybe(rng, 0.2):
            frag.append(rng.choice(" "))
            frag.append(_rand_from(rng, HEX, 2))
        # Optional trailing spaces
        if _maybe(rng, 0.5):
            frag.append(_rand_from(rng, ASCII_WHITESPACE, rng.randint(0, 5)))
        fields.append(''.join(frag))

    # Join with a rotating set of delimiters (comma, colon, space, tab, pipe)
    delims = [",", ":", " ", "\t", "|", ";"]
    s = []
    for i, f in enumerate(fields):
        if i:
            d = rng.choice(delims)
            # Sometimes double delimiters
            if _maybe(rng, 0.25):
                d = d * rng.randint(1, 3)
            s.append(d)
        s.append(f)

    # Optional trailing whitespace and punctuation
    if _maybe(rng, 0.8):
        s.append(_rand_from(rng, ASCII_WHITESPACE, rng.randint(0, 8)))
    if _maybe(rng, 0.3):
        s.append(_rand_from(rng, ":;.,", rng.randint(0, 3)))

    base = ''.join(s)

    # Ensure presence of ':' periodically for percent_escape tests
    if ':' not in base and _maybe(rng, 0.7):
        insert_pos = rng.randint(0, len(base))
        base = base[:insert_pos] + ":" + base[insert_pos:]

    # Bound length
    if len(base.encode('utf-8')) > target_len:
        # Truncate by characters, then ensure no split in the middle of multi-byte
        trimmed = base.encode('utf-8')[:target_len]
        # Fix potential cut UTF-8 by backing up to a valid boundary
        while trimmed and (trimmed[-1] & 0xC0) == 0x80:
            trimmed = trimmed[:-1]
        base = trimmed.decode('utf-8', errors='ignore')

    # Allow empty string occasionally
    if _maybe(rng, 0.1):
        base = ""

    return base

def _make_char_set(rng: random.Random, include_ws_bias: float = 0.5) -> str:
    charset = []
    # Sometimes include ASCII whitespace
    if _maybe(rng, include_ws_bias):
        charset.append(_rand_from(rng, ASCII_WHITESPACE, rng.randint(1, 4)))
    # Common trim characters
    candidates = ":;,.|/\\-_\"'()[]{}\t \n\r\f\v"
    charset.append(_rand_from(rng, candidates, rng.randint(0, 6)))
    # Sometimes include digits or hex to test generic trimming
    if _maybe(rng, 0.3):
        charset.append(_rand_from(rng, string.digits, rng.randint(1, 3)))
    # De-duplicate while preserving order
    seen = set()
    out = []
    for ch in ''.join(charset):
        if ch not in seen and ch != '\0':
            seen.add(ch)
            out.append(ch)
    # Allow empty set occasionally
    if not out and _maybe(rng, 0.5):
        out.append(' ')
    return ''.join(out)

def _make_delim_set(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Build a set for strsep/strtokenize and strpbrk
    base_candidates = ",;:|/\\\t \n\r\f\v.\-_=+\0"  # include many common delimiters
    # Ensure not to include NUL since C-strings end at NUL; it would truncate
    base_candidates = base_candidates.replace('\0', '')
    s = []
    # Always include at least one delimiter
    s.append(rng.choice(",:|; \t\n"))
    # Add a few more unique ones
    for _ in range(rng.randint(0, 6)):
        ch = rng.choice(base_candidates)
        if ch not in s:
            s.append(ch)
    # Sometimes return a single-char delimiter, sometimes longer set
    return ''.join(s)

def _make_extra_escape_set(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Extra characters to percent-escape beyond ':'
    # Focus on characters often escaped in URIs/paths
    pool = " /?#[]@!$&'()*+,;=\t\n\r%\\\""
    # Sometimes empty (caller might pass NULL, but harness decides that)
    if _maybe(rng, 0.2):
        return ""
    n = rng.randint(1, 8)
    # Unique characters only
    seen = set()
    out = []
    while len(out) < n:
        ch = rng.choice(pool)
        if ch not in seen:
            seen.add(ch)
            out.append(ch)
    return ''.join(out)


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Target overall size <= 4096. Allocate about 3 KB for S0 and the rest small.
    s0 = _make_general_text(rng, target_len=3072)
    s1 = _make_char_set(rng, include_ws_bias=0.7)
    s2 = _make_delim_set(rng)
    s3 = _make_extra_escape_set(rng)

    # Ensure they are valid UTF-8 strings and do not contain embedded NUL
    def sanitize(s: str) -> str:
        return s.replace('\0', '')

    s0 = sanitize(s0)
    s1 = sanitize(s1)
    s2 = sanitize(s2)
    s3 = sanitize(s3)

    parts = [s0, s1, s2, s3]
    blob = b"\0".join(p.encode('utf-8') for p in parts) + b"\0"

    # Final size guard
    if len(blob) > 4096:
        blob = blob[:4096]
        # Ensure it ends with NUL to properly terminate last string
        if blob[-1] != 0:
            # Trim back to last NUL if present, else append a NUL (and drop one byte)
            last_nul = blob.rfind(b"\0")
            if last_nul == -1:
                blob = blob[:-1] + b"\0"
            else:
                blob = blob[:last_nul + 1]

    return blob

import random
import string
from typing import List

# This generator targets fuzzers that consume filepath strings via FUZZ_PARAM_STR.
# We construct a single bytes buffer that encodes multiple interesting NUL-terminated
# strings concatenated together. The fuzzing harness will slice from this pool to
# initialize different parameters.
#
# Goals:
# - Include Windows and POSIX path variants
# - Mix absolute/relative, dot/dotdot, trailing slashes, UNC, device paths
# - Include paths with spaces, unicode, percent chars, colons, multiple separators
# - Include empty string and single NUL to test edge cases
# - Keep under 4096 bytes

MAX_TOTAL = 4096

ASCII_SAFE = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "-_ ."

UNICODE_SAMPLES = [
    "ümlaut",                # Latin-1
    "漢字",                  # CJK
    "файл",                 # Cyrillic
    "नाम",                  # Devanagari
    "파일",                 # Hangul
    "🙂",                    # Emoji
]

WIN_DRIVES = [f"{ch}:" for ch in string.ascii_uppercase]

POSIX_ROOTS = ["/", "/.", "/..", "/tmp", "/var/log", "/home/user", "/etc", "/dev/null"]
WIN_ROOTS = [
    d + "\\" for d in WIN_DRIVES[:6]
] + [
    r"\\\\server\\share",            # UNC
    r"\\\\?\\C:\\",                # Win32 device namespace
    r"\\\\.\\C:\\",                # DOS device path
]

SPECIAL_SEGMENTS = [".", "..", "...", " ", "-", "_", "~", "%20", "#", "@", "+", "=", ":", ";"]

EXTS = ["", ".txt", ".conf", ".gpg", ".asc", ".bin", ".dat", ".log", ".", ".😀"]

FILENAMES_BASE = [
    "",                      # empty filename
    "a", "A", "0", "file", "File", "README", "Makefile",
    "con", "nul", "prn",   # Windows reserved names
    "aux", "clock$", "com1", "lpt9",
    "with space", "leading space ", " trailing space",
    "dots...", ".hidden", "..doublehidden", "name.with.many.dots",
    "percent:colon", "colon:here", "semi;colon", "hash#tag",
    *UNICODE_SAMPLES,
]

def rand_choice(rng: random.Random, seq: List[str]) -> str:
    return seq[rng.randrange(len(seq))]

def rand_ascii(rng: random.Random, min_len=1, max_len=16) -> str:
    n = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    return ''.join(rng.choice(ASCII_SAFE) for _ in range(n))

def join_posix(parts: List[str]) -> str:
    # Ensure single slashes; keep empty parts to trigger // or trailing /
    s = parts[0]
    for p in parts[1:]:
        if not s.endswith('/'):
            s += '/'
        s += p
    return s

def join_win(parts: List[str]) -> str:
    s = parts[0]
    for p in parts[1:]:
        if not s.endswith('\\'):
            s += '\\'
        s += p
    return s

def make_posix_path(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    root = rng.choice([True, False])
    segments = []
    depth = rng.randint(0, 6)
    for _ in range(depth):
        choice = rng.randint(0, 5)
        if choice == 0:
            seg = rand_ascii(rng)
        elif choice == 1:
            seg = rand_choice(rng, SPECIAL_SEGMENTS)
        elif choice == 2:
            seg = rand_choice(rng, FILENAMES_BASE)
        elif choice == 3:
            seg = rand_ascii(rng, 1, 3) + ":" + rand_ascii(rng, 1, 3)
        elif choice == 4:
            seg = rand_choice(rng, UNICODE_SAMPLES)
        else:
            seg = str(rng.randint(0, 999))
        if rng.random() < 0.3:
            seg += rand_choice(rng, EXTS)
        segments.append(seg)
    if root:
        base = rand_choice(rng, POSIX_ROOTS)
        parts = [base.rstrip('/') or '/'] + segments
        path = join_posix(parts)
    else:
        prefix = rng.choice(["", "./", "../", "../../", "././/"])  # include redundant slashes
        path = prefix + (join_posix([segments[0]] + segments[1:]) if segments else rand_choice(rng, FILENAMES_BASE))
    if rng.random() < 0.4:
        path += "/"
    return path

def make_windows_path(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    base = rand_choice(rng, WIN_ROOTS)
    depth = rng.randint(0, 6)
    segs = []
    for _ in range(depth):
        choice = rng.randint(0, 5)
        if choice == 0:
            seg = rand_ascii(rng)
        elif choice == 1:
            seg = rand_choice(rng, SPECIAL_SEGMENTS)
        elif choice == 2:
            seg = rand_choice(rng, FILENAMES_BASE)
        elif choice == 3:
            seg = rand_ascii(rng, 1, 3) + ":" + rand_ascii(rng, 1, 3)
        elif choice == 4:
            seg = rand_choice(rng, UNICODE_SAMPLES)
        else:
            seg = str(rng.randint(0, 999))
        if rng.random() < 0.3:
            seg += rand_choice(rng, EXTS)
        segs.append(seg)
    path = join_win([base.rstrip('\\')] + segs) if segs else base
    if rng.random() < 0.4:
        path += "\\"
    # Optionally add mixed separators to stress normalization
    if rng.random() < 0.2:
        path = path.replace('\\', '/').replace('//', '/')
    return path

def make_mixed_path(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Create intentionally mixed but still usable strings (not malformed):
    # E.g., C:/Program Files/GnuPG/bin, //server/share/dir, /mnt/c/Windows
    options = []
    options.append("C:/Program Files/GnuPG/bin")
    options.append("/mnt/c/Windows/System32")
    options.append("//server/share/folder/file.txt")
    options.append("/home/user/.gnupg/pubring.kbx")
    options.append(r"\\\\server\\share\\folder\\file.txt")
    options.append("..//relative//path/./to//file")
    return rand_choice(rng, options)

def make_filename_pair_pool(rng: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    # For compare_filenames(a,b) and make_basename(fp, ip) we want combinations
    # that differ only by case, trailing slashes, dot segments, UNC vs drive, etc.
    paths = []
    # Edge cases
    paths.append("")
    paths.append("\0")  # stand-alone NUL for robustness; will be split as empty
    paths.extend([".", "..", "/", "\\", ".\\", "./", "../", "..\\"])

    # POSIX and Windows examples
    for _ in range(8):
        paths.append(make_posix_path(rng))
        paths.append(make_windows_path(rng))
        paths.append(make_mixed_path(rng))

    # Case variants
    base = "C:/Users/Example/Desktop/File.TXT"
    paths.append(base)
    paths.append(base.lower())
    paths.append(base.upper())

    # Trailing slash variants
    for p in ["/tmp/test", "C:/Temp/test"]:
        paths.append(p)
        paths.append(p + "/")
        paths.append(p + "\\")

    # Names with colons for percent_escape interplay in upstream
    paths.append("keyring:default")
    paths.append("C:/path:with:colons/file")

    # Unicode combinations
    for u in UNICODE_SAMPLES[:3]:
        paths.append(f"/home/{u}/Док")
        paths.append(f"C:/Программы/{u}")

    # Very long but under limit
    long_seg = "a" * rng.randint(50, 150)
    paths.append("/var/log/" + long_seg + ".log")
    paths.append("C:/" + long_seg + ".dat")

    # Paths with multiple separators
    paths.append("/usr//local///bin////gpg")
    paths.append("C:\\Program Files\\\\GnuPG\\bin\\gpg.exe")

    return paths


def encode_c_string(s: str) -> bytes:
    # Input is a Python str; encode as UTF-8 and terminate with NUL
    # If the string contains an embedded NUL marker ("\0"), interpret it as literal NUL insertion.
    # This allows us to include empty strings and edge cases explicitly.
    raw = bytearray()
    i = 0
    while i < len(s):
        if s[i] == '\\' and i + 1 < len(s) and s[i+1] == '0':
            raw.append(0)
            i += 2
        else:
            raw.extend(s[i].encode('utf-8'))
            i += 1
    raw.append(0)
    return bytes(raw)


def build_pool(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Construct a pool of NUL-terminated strings concatenated together.
    parts: List[bytes] = []

    # Filename pairs and general paths
    for s in make_filename_pair_pool(rng):
        parts.append(encode_c_string(s))

    # Input path hints for make_basename second arg: include prefixes/suffixes
    hints = [
        "", ".", "..", "/", "./", "../", "~", "~user", "C:", "C:/", r"\\\\server\\share",
        "/home/user", "/home/user/", "/home/user/.gnupg/", "C:/Users/User", "C:/Users/User/",
        "../relative/base", "/var/lib/gnupg", "/etc/gnupg", "/usr/local/bin",
    ]
    for h in hints:
        parts.append(encode_c_string(h))

    blob = b"".join(parts)
    # Truncate to MAX_TOTAL safely by ensuring we end at a NUL boundary
    if len(blob) > MAX_TOTAL:
        blob = blob[:MAX_TOTAL]
        # Ensure last byte is NUL to keep final string terminated
        if blob[-1] != 0:
            # Backtrack to previous NUL; if none, force append NUL by trimming
            idx = blob.rfind(b"\x00")
            if idx != -1:
                blob = blob[:idx+1]
            else:
                # If no NUL found (unlikely), ensure minimal valid C-string
                blob = b"\x00"
    return blob


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    return build_pool(rng)

import os
import random
import string
from typing import List

# Generator for valid filepath component strings suitable for make_filename and make_absfilename stubs.
# FUZZ_PARAM_STR pulls from the single input buffer; common harnesses split on NULs to form multiple strings.
# We therefore construct a byte buffer containing multiple NUL-terminated path components, plus an unsigned int
# (for the selector) if the harness expects it from the same buffer. Many libFuzzer-style helpers do this.
# Our strategy:
# - Produce 3-5 NUL-terminated components with diverse semantics:
#   * empty component ""
#   * simple names
#   * names with dots, spaces
#   * names with path separators for different OSes (but still as components; some APIs may treat them literally)
#   * names with percent-escapes and UTF-8
#   * Windows drive-like prefixes (as components) and UNC-like parts
# - Ensure overall size <= 4096 bytes.
# - Append a 4-byte little-endian unsigned int selector to exercise which-branch in stubs.
# - Include both relative-looking and absolute-looking first components so make_absfilename can form absolute paths.
#   Although the API ensures absoluteness, the inputs influence normalization.

MAX_TOTAL = 4096

ASCII = string.ascii_letters + string.digits
SAFE_CHARS = ASCII + "-_., "

def _rand_rng(seed: int) -> random.Random:
    return random.Random(seed)

def _pick(rng: random.Random, seq):
    return seq[rng.randrange(len(seq))]

def _rand_ascii_name(rng: random.Random, min_len=1, max_len=16) -> str:
    n = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    return ''.join(_pick(rng, SAFE_CHARS) for _ in range(n)).strip()

def _rand_utf8_name(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Mix ASCII with some common multi-byte UTF-8 sequences
    pool = [
        "naïve", "café", "résumé", "über", "fiancé", "mañana",
        "日本語", "русский", "ελληνικά", "한국어", "中文",
        "😀", "📁", "Δelta", "Ångström", "SãoPaulo"
    ]
    base = _pick(rng, pool)
    suffix = _rand_ascii_name(rng, 0, 6)
    return (base + suffix)[:32]

def _rand_ext(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    return _pick(rng, [".txt", ".bin", ".cfg", ".dat", ".log", ".gpg", ".asc", ".tar.gz"]) 

def _percenty(rng: random.Random, s: str) -> str:
    # Introduce chars interesting for percent_escape, but keep valid component
    extras = [":", "%", "#", "+", "?", "&", "="]
    if rng.random() < 0.6:
        s = s + _pick(rng, extras)
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        s += "%3a"
    return s

def _maybe_separators(rng: random.Random, s: str) -> str:
    # Include slashes or backslashes as literal characters within a component occasionally
    # to exercise handling; still a single C string component.
    if not s:
        s = _rand_ascii_name(rng, 1, 4)
    inserts = ["/", "//", "\\", "..", ".", "~"]
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        pos = rng.randrange(1, len(s)+1)
        s = s[:pos] + _pick(rng, inserts) + s[pos:]
    return s

def _windowsy_parts(rng: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    # Components that look Windows-like but are individual parts
    drives = ["C:", "D:", "Z:"]
    unc = ["\\\x5cserver", "\\server", "server", "share"]  # literal backslashes
    # We will produce strings with backslashes; Python strings need escaping
    return [
        _pick(rng, drives),
        "Users",
        _rand_ascii_name(rng, 3, 8),
        _rand_ascii_name(rng, 2, 6) + _rand_ext(rng)
    ]

def _unixy_parts(rng: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    roots = ["/", "//", "/home", "/etc", "/var", "/tmp"]
    return [
        _pick(rng, roots),
        _rand_ascii_name(rng, 2, 8),
        _rand_ascii_name(rng, 2, 8) + _rand_ext(rng)
    ]

def _build_components(rng: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    comps: List[str] = []
    style = rng.choice(["unix", "win", "relative", "mixed"]) 

    if style == "unix":
        comps.extend(_unixy_parts(rng))
    elif style == "win":
        comps.extend(_windowsy_parts(rng))
    elif style == "relative":
        comps.append(_pick(rng, [".", "..", "", _rand_ascii_name(rng,1,6)]))
        comps.append(_rand_ascii_name(rng, 1, 10))
        comps.append(_rand_ascii_name(rng, 1, 10) + _rand_ext(rng))
    else:  # mixed
        comps.append(_pick(rng, ["/", "", ".", "..", "~"]))
        comps.append(_maybe_separators(rng, _percenty(rng, _rand_ascii_name(rng, 1, 8))))
        comps.append(_rand_utf8_name(rng) + ("" if rng.random()<0.5 else _rand_ext(rng)))

    # Randomly insert an empty component to hit edge case branch
    if rng.random() < 0.4:
        insert_pos = rng.randrange(0, min(3, len(comps))+1)
        comps.insert(insert_pos, "")

    # Add a couple more interesting tail components optionally
    tails = []
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        tails.append(_maybe_separators(rng, _percenty(rng, "config")))
    if rng.random() < 0.3:
        tails.append("..")
    comps.extend(tails)

    # Ensure at least 3 components as stubs use up to p1, p2, p3
    while len(comps) < 3:
        comps.append(_rand_ascii_name(rng, 1, 6))

    # Limit excessive size
    limited = []
    total = 0
    for c in comps:
        c = c[:128]
        if total + len(c) + 1 > MAX_TOTAL - 8:  # leave room for selector
            break
        limited.append(c)
        total += len(c) + 1
    return limited

def _pack_u32_le(x: int) -> bytes:
    return bytes((x & 0xFF, (x >> 8) & 0xFF, (x >> 16) & 0xFF, (x >> 24) & 0xFF))

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = _rand_rng(seed)

    comps = _build_components(rng)

    # Build several scenarios in one buffer to satisfy multiple FUZZ_PARAM_STR() calls:
    # We will concatenate components with NUL terminators so each FUZZ_PARAM_STR can pull the next string.
    payload = bytearray()

    # Shuffle a copy sometimes to vary pairings across calls
    order = comps[:]
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        rng.shuffle(order)

    for s in order[:5]:  # up to 5 components provided
        try:
            b = s.encode('utf-8')
        except Exception:
            b = s.encode('utf-8', errors='replace')
        payload += b + b"\x00"

    # Append a selector for which-branch choices in stubs (modulo used in code)
    selector = rng.randrange(0, 4)
    payload += _pack_u32_le(selector)

    # Ensure size limit
    if len(payload) > MAX_TOTAL:
        payload = payload[:MAX_TOTAL]

    return bytes(payload)
